albums.blurb: Penguin Cafe Orchestra was the London ensemble of composer Simon Jeffes, founded in 1972 to make music that ignored the border between chamber music and folk; their 1976 debut appeared on Brian Eno's Obscure label. This self-titled second album, recorded between 1977 and 1980 and released on E.G. Records, became the group's signature: fifteen entirely instrumental miniatures for ukulele, violin, cuatro and piano, including "Telephone and Rubber Band," built on the looped ring of an engaged phone line.
albums.reception: Robert Christgau graded the album A−, and in 2021 Spin named it among the fifty best albums of 1981.

albums.blurb: Dr. Dog are a Philadelphia band built around the twin songwriting of bassist Toby Leaman and guitarist Scott McMicken, long known for recording their Beatles- and Band-indebted harmonies in their own home studio. Fate, released in 2008 on Park the Van between We All Belong (2007) and Shame, Shame (2010), thickens their lo-fi psych-pop with horns, strings and gospel-tinged piano; its closer "My Friend" later turned up in the trailers for Judd Apatow's Funny People.
albums.reception: Entertainment Weekly graded the album A− and Rolling Stone gave it three and a half stars out of five.

albums.blurb: Khruangbin — Thai for "airplane" — are a Houston trio of bassist Laura Lee, guitarist Mark Speer and drummer DJ Johnson whose largely instrumental sound filters surf and soul through the Thai funk cassettes that first inspired them. Con Todo el Mundo, their second album, released in January 2018 on Dead Oceans and Night Time Stories, widens the palette of their 2015 debut The Universe Smiles upon You with Mediterranean and Middle Eastern influences; the title comes from a phrase of Lee's Mexican grandfather.
albums.reception: The album holds a Metacritic score of 78 out of 100 based on 13 critic reviews, indicating generally favorable reviews.
